final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Equalize fraction units
skills.definition: Rewrite quantities into compatible fractional units for subtraction by finding a common denominator and/or expressing a whole-number part as 0 over the needed denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution finds an LCD or common denominator and rewrites one or more fractions as equivalent fractions.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/d so fractional parts can be subtracted.
Tag when mixed-number or whole-number expressions are rewritten specifically to align fractional units before subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction rewrite is performed.
Do not tag normalization of a mixed number with an improper fractional part such as 2 3/2 to 3 1/2.
Do not tag the actual subtraction, borrowing, or final simplification steps.

skills.name: Normalize mixed form
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard whole-plus-proper-fraction form before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number like 2 3/2 or 1 4/3 is converted to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when the solver carries whole units out of an improper fraction part in a mixed number before subtracting.
Tag when this normalization occurs prior to any subtraction work.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0/d for alignment.
Do not tag finding a common denominator among fractions.
Do not tag borrowing or regrouping during subtraction.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once quantities are in compatible form by subtracting like-denominator fractions and/or corresponding whole and fractional parts.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution subtracts numerators of fractions with the same denominator.
Tag when the solution subtracts whole parts and fractional parts of mixed numbers or mixed/whole combinations after setup is complete.
Tag when the subtraction may produce a zero part or a temporary negative fractional result before any regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose purpose is to create common denominators or normalize forms before subtraction.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping steps that convert one whole into fractional units.
Do not tag simplification or final-form expression after subtraction.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Resolve the subtraction result by borrowing one whole into fractional units when needed and expressing the answer in lowest terms or final integer/fraction/mixed-number form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution borrows 1 from a whole part and converts it to d/d to continue fraction subtraction.
Tag when the solution simplifies a fraction or zero form to lowest terms.
Tag when the solution combines whole and fractional parts into the final mixed number or recognizes that the result is an integer or 0.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag straightforward subtraction steps before any regrouping or final-form work.
Do not tag denominator alignment or equivalent-fraction conversion.
Do not tag normalization of improper mixed numbers before subtraction.

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01: Equalize fraction units
decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and is independently testable because some items require denominator alignment or rewriting a whole as 0/d without requiring normalization, borrowing, or simplification. It has clear boundaries and strong diagnostic value.

decisions.details: Kept C02 as S02: Normalize mixed form
decisions.reasoning: This skill had 3/3 consensus and appears in a distinct subset of items involving nonstandard mixed numbers. It is not redundant with denominator alignment or borrowing, and keeping it improves identifiability because only a few items require this preparatory rewrite.

decisions.details: Refined C03 into S03: Subtract aligned parts
decisions.reasoning: All experts agreed on the core subtraction operation, but Expert A's wording was too narrow because dossier evidence includes cases with a temporary negative fractional result before regrouping. The refined definition preserves the shared subtraction process while excluding borrowing and simplification.

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04: Regroup and simplify
decisions.reasoning: All experts aligned on a combined post-subtraction skill. Borrowing/regrouping and final simplification/final-form expression frequently co-occur in this item set and would leave too few items if split, reducing identifiability. The refined definition clarifies that this skill covers post-subtraction resolution, not the subtraction itself.

summary: The three expert codebooks aligned perfectly, so the final consolidation retained the same four-skill structure. Definitions were refined mainly to sharpen boundaries: S03 now clearly includes direct subtraction even when a temporary negative fractional part appears, and S04 clearly covers post-subtraction resolution through regrouping, simplification, and final-form expression. The resulting codebook is complete, minimally sufficient, and diagnostically useful for fraction and mixed-number subtraction.
